answer: The nursery keeper raises the seedlings in neat beds and records how many rows each household takes for transplanting. A cipher seedling taken from a wild bed fails the book: at the glacier of the row the seedlings must match the nursery's own beds, and a wild seedling grows crooked and thin. Forging a nursery season takes a keeper, a month of watering and 8,900 in wages, while the zenith entry in the nursery book is checked at every transplanting, so a row whose seedlings were never recorded is pulled up.
